title: Returns & Exchanges Restocking Fee on Grade B Units
content:
This calculation sheet sets the Returns & Exchanges restocking fee withheld on an order line whose units were graded B (unworn, tags detached) at inspection.

## Calculation

1. **Line and units.** The line charged is the order line whose inspection entries show units graded B; its units graded B are the units on those entries.
2. **Merchandise credit per accepted unit.** The merchandise part of the line's credit entry, divided by the line's accepted units (the units on its inspection entries with the outcome accepted or accepted with fee).
3. **Restocking fee per unit.** The return type's grade B restocking percentage of the merchandise credit per accepted unit, rounded half up to the cent; that figure is then capped at the return type's restocking fee cap per unit, and is never larger than the merchandise credit per accepted unit.
4. **Fee withheld.** The restocking fee per unit times the line's units graded B, rounded half up to the cent.

Half-up rounding in this calculation is applied with a tolerance of 0.0001 cent, so an amount lying on a half cent always goes up.

## Worked examples (hypothetical figures; return type with a 15 percent grade B percentage and a 30.00 USD cap per unit)

| Step | Example A | Example B |
|---|---|---|
| Merchandise part of the credit entry | 179.98 for 2 accepted units | 450.00 for 2 accepted units |
| Merchandise credit per accepted unit | 89.99 | 225.00 |
| 15 percent of it | 13.4985, rounded half up to 13.50 | 33.75 |
| After the 30.00 cap and the per-unit ceiling | 13.50 | 30.00 |
| Units graded B | 1 | 2 |
| Fee withheld | 13.50 | 60.00 |

## Points of judgement

- A line with 3 units accepted, 1 of them graded B: the merchandise credit per accepted unit is taken over all 3 accepted units, and the fee is charged on the 1 unit graded B.
- A fee per unit can never exceed what was credited per accepted unit, whatever the percentage gives.
